answer: Each submission hangs on the shale of a task receipt, and the lantern is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, re-queued for a second panel, rewards vest against future work. The plume of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short.
